cover: Use case: illustration-story. Create an original wide editorial cover for a technical article, aspect ratio 2.4:1. Headline at left in large classic dark navy serif type, exact text: "Passing once is not the same as being reliable". Smaller subtitle: "What repeated attempts tell us about AI evals". At right, an elegant nineteenth-century mechanical ticket press on an engineer's desk, with a long folded paper strip of four separate attempt tickets passing through it. Two tickets bear cobalt blue checkmarks and two bear vermilion crosses. The device is a metaphor for checking the same task repeatedly, not a computer or robot. Warm ivory paper, precise navy pen-and-ink hatching, restrained cobalt, vermilion and ochre accents, fine drafting lines, generous margins, classic book illustration. Distinct original composition. No charts, extra text, robot, dashboard, rounded UI cards, gradients, watermark or signature. Text must be legible, no punctuation dashes.
pairs: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a wide landscape editorial diagram, approximately 1.8:1, titled "The same attempts, two different questions". Warm ivory paper, precise navy pen-and-ink technical hatching, classic large serif typography, generous margins, restrained cobalt blue pass checkmarks and vermilion fail crosses, ochre thin rules. Match illustrated engineering notebook, not UI dashboard. Top: four clearly separate paper specimen tickets in order: A with blue checkmark, B with red cross, C with blue checkmark, D with red cross. Small caption: "Four recorded attempts". Middle: exactly six distinct two-ticket pairs arranged horizontally, with labels AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD. Show symbols strictly: AB check cross; AC check check; AD check cross; BC cross check; BD cross cross; CD check cross. Do not add pairs. Bottom left an open inspection ledger with exact heading "At least one passes" and caption "5 of 6 pairs". Bottom right second ledger heading "Both pass" and caption "1 of 6 pairs". No arrows crossing, no extra percentages, no mathematical notation, no other words. Clear typesetting and large symbols, diagrams front-facing and easy to read. Aesthetic is hand-engraved scientific journal, restrained decoration; no robots, rounded cards, shadows, gradients, signatures, logos or watermark.
